reason: Fresh research today confirms rather than undermines this book's core theses, and the FOMC event itself is not a repositioning catalyst -- fed-funds futures imply roughly a 90% probability of a hold at 3.75-4.00% tomorrow, so no surprise is priced to react to. The energy leg's thesis is playing out in real time: XOM is +41.7% YTD at $167, refining margins are at record highs, Exxon just landed a $200m PNG LNG contract via Wood, and Piper Sandler raised its target to $185. UNH -- the book's largest leg and its worst performer on paper at -4.48% -- just got the exact fundamental turn this deep-value mandate is built to catch: raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $19.50-$20.00 on improving medical-cost trends plus JPMorgan lifting its price target to $516; selling that now would mean exiting the thesis just as it starts confirming. The real headwind found today is the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.01% (highest since 2007 and still climbing), which pressures the IWM small-cap-value leg and compounds Ford's already-negative operating margins (-3.7%, ~$8.2B projected FY loss) -- but those are the two smallest legs (6% and 4%), both already carry stops, and a full-book replacement would spend real bps fixing marginal legs while the 41% of the book in XOM/UNH/GM/JPM is intact or improving. The 40% cash buffer stays as dry powder to add to XOM/UNH strength or weakness rather than being deployed reactively into a Fed decision that is already priced in.
